ours.name: Washington Ellinor Traverse (Ridge)
ours.approach: Climb Mount Washington first via its standard south route from the FR 2419 trailhead (see the Standard Route). The traverse itself has no separate trailhead or approach — it begins directly from Washington's summit, heading southwest along the connecting ridge toward Mt. Ellinor rather than descending Washington's standard route.
ours.descent: Most parties continue the traverse to Mount Ellinor's summit and descend via Mount Ellinor's standard trail (upper trailhead off a spur of FR-2419, the same North Lake Cushman Road corridor used for the approach); parties can also reverse the traverse back over Mount Washington to its own trailhead.

fktText: Description Start at the Mt Washington trailhead, which is nearby the mt ellinor trailheads. it starts off super steep and stays that way the entire time. It starts forested, then there is a scree field crossing. After that, there is another short forested section before coming into a meadow. Then, you continue on another scree field, before starting the scrambling section. You walk up a switchback, and then walk along the ridge for a little while. When almost at the summit, stay right and go around the right side of a boulder, and then the summit is right there.
